The function is defined at `backend/app/crud.py:34`. It takes keyword-only `session` and `email` arguments and returns `User | None`. Application code calls it from 8 places. The other callers are in tests (`backend/tests/utils/user.py:39` and `backend/tests/api/routes/test_users.py`).

**`backend/app/crud.py`**
- `authenticate` (`:46`) uses the result to verify the password. If the result is `None`, it verifies against `DUMMY_HASH` to keep timing constant (`:50`). Otherwise it reads `hashed_password` and may rehash and commit it (`:52-59`).

**`backend/app/api/routes/login.py`**
- `recover_password` (`:58`) only checks whether the user exists. If so, it uses `user.email` to send a reset email (`:62-71`). It returns the same response either way.
- `reset_password` (`:85`) returns 400 if the user is missing or `not user.is_active` (`:86-90`). Otherwise it passes the object to `crud.update_user` as `db_user` (`:92-96`).
- `recover_password_html_content` (`:109`) returns 404 if the user is missing. Otherwise it uses `user.email` to build the email HTML (`:111-119`).

**`backend/app/api/routes/users.py`**
- Create-user route (`:61`) only checks existence and returns 400 if the email is taken (`:62-66`).
- Update-own-profile route (`:90`) checks for an email conflict. It returns 409 if `existing_user.id != current_user.id` (`:91-94`).
- Signup route (`:151`) only checks existence and returns 400 if the email is taken (`:152-156`).
- Admin update-user route (`:204`) checks for an email conflict. It returns 409 if `existing_user.id != user_id` (`:205-208`).

**Impact on a signature change**
- All callers use keyword arguments (`session=`, `email=`), so renaming or reordering parameters is safe. Renaming them breaks every call site.
- Four callers only test truthiness: `users.py:61`, `users.py:151`, `login.py:58` and `login.py:109`, apart from the `user.email` reads in the two login routes.
- Two callers read `.id` (`users.py:91`, `:205`).
- Three callers need the full `User` object: `authenticate` (`:46`), `reset_password` (`:85`) and the `login.py` callers that read `.email`. `authenticate` and `reset_password` need it for `hashed_password`, `is_active` and `update_user`.
- If you change the return type, for example to raise instead of returning `None`, every `if user` / `if not user` branch has to change. That includes the timing-attack and anti-enumeration paths in `authenticate` and `recover_password`.
